scenes.title: Explanation — the 10 rules
items: Bookmark the sites you use; never reach them from ads, DMs or emails.
Nobody legitimate DMs you first offering help, investments or "recovery".
Read every wallet prompt before approving
scenes.vo: First, never share your seed phrase. No real person or company will ever ask for it. Next, Bookmark the sites you use; never reach them from ads, DMs or emails. Then, Nobody legitimate DMs you first offering help, investments or "recovery". Also, Guaranteed returns are a scam. Always. On top of that, Read every wallet prompt before approving: what, how much, to whom.

scenes.title: Explanation — the 10 rules (cont.)
items: Test first with a small amount on anything new.
Use a hardware wallet once the amount matters to you.
Keep devices updated, and use a separate browser profile for crypto.
Keep records of every buy, sell, transfer and fee.
scenes.vo: And Test first with a small amount on anything new. Plus, use a hardware wallet once the amount matters to you. One more: keep devices updated, and use a separate browser profile for crypto. One more: keep records of every buy, sell, transfer and fee. And finally, if something feels urgent, stop. Scammers create urgency; real opportunities wait.

scenes.title: Glossary (the words you'll meet next)
scenes.vo: Address: your public "account number" on a blockchain. Seed phrase: 12 to 24 words that recreate your wallet's keys. Never share. Private key: the secret that signs transactions (your seed phrase generates it). Custody: who holds the keys: an exchange (custodial) or you (self-custody). Gas: the network fee for a transaction, paid in the network's token. Network or chain: A blockchain, for example Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base.
scenes.cap: Address: your public "account number" on a blockchain. Seed phrase: 12–24 words that recreate your wallet's keys. Never share. Private key: the secret that signs transactions (your seed phrase generates it). Custody: who holds the keys: an exchange (custodial) or you (self-custody). Gas: the network fee for a transaction, paid in the network's token. Network / chain: A blockchain, e.g. Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base.

scenes.title: Glossary (the words you'll meet next)
scenes.vo: Layer 2 (layer two): A cheaper, faster network built on top of Ethereum. Token: A unit of value on a blockchain, for example U.S.D.C. Stablecoin: A token designed to hold a steady value, usually $1. Smart contract: A program on a blockchain that follows fixed rules. decks: Decentralised exchange: swap tokens from your wallet. Approval: Permission for an app to move a specific token.
scenes.cap: Layer 2 (L2): A cheaper, faster network built on top of Ethereum. Token: A unit of value on a blockchain, e.g. USDC. Stablecoin: A token designed to hold a steady value, usually $1. Smart contract: A program on a blockchain that follows fixed rules. DEX: Decentralised exchange: swap tokens from your wallet. Approval: Permission for an app to move a specific token.

scenes.title: Glossary (the words you'll meet next)
scenes.vo: Block explorer: A website that shows every transaction (for example Etherscan). Testnet or faucet: A practice blockchain or a site giving free test coins. A.P.Y.: Annual percentage yield: yearly return including compounding. Liquidity: how easily something can be bought or sold without moving the price. K.Y.C.: ID checks required by regulated exchanges. two-factor: Two-factor authentication: a second proof of identity at login.
scenes.cap: Block explorer: A website that shows every transaction (e.g. Etherscan). Testnet / faucet: A practice blockchain / a site giving free test coins. APY: Annual percentage yield: yearly return including compounding. Liquidity: how easily something can be bought or sold without moving the price. KYC: ID checks required by regulated exchanges. 2FA: Two-factor authentication: a second proof of identity at login.

scenes.q: A message says your wallet will be "suspended" unless you act in 1 hour. What do you do?
scenes.a: Stop. Urgency is a scam tactic. Wallets can't be suspended; check only through bookmarked official sites.

scenes.title: Part A — Accounts (≈ 45 min)

Authenticator app installed on your phone
Exchange chosen (legally available to you, reputable)
Exchange account opened and KYC completed
